text:
Help me write an announcement to our staff. I'm the COO of a credit union with 7 branches. We're closing the Maple Street and Route 9 branches on March 31 and moving the people who work there to a new member phone and chat center.

Facts:
- The two branches have 14 staff between them. Every one of them is offered a job in the phone and chat center at the same pay or higher.
- Visits to those two branches fell 44% over the last three years. Phone and chat contacts across the credit union went up 60%.
- Members calling us now wait an average of 9 minutes on hold.
- The center will be open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. The branches were open 9 to 5. Shifts will rotate.
- Staff in the center can work from home two days a week after 90 days of training.
- Anyone who doesn't take the new role gets 2 weeks of pay for every year they've worked here.

I want the announcement to say that this change will make everyone's job better. About 400 words, sent by email from me.

Before I draft, a few questions. The answers would change what the email says:

1. **Who gets this email, and have the 14 already heard?** Is it going to all staff, or only the people at Maple Street and Route 9? Will those 14 have been told in person before it goes out? Learning about your own branch closing from a company-wide email lands very differently from getting it as a follow-up.

2. **What actually gets better, and for whom?** The 14 are trading a 9-to-5 schedule for rotating shifts that can run until 8 p.m. Unless the email names concrete gains, many of them will read "better" as spin. Gains could include higher pay for some, working from home, training or a career path, or no longer facing slow, empty branches. What would you point to? For the other five branches, is there a real gain to name, like fewer transferred calls or shorter waits for their members?

3. **Where is the center, and when does it open?** Will people commute somewhere new? Does training start before March 31?

4. **What's the decision process?** When do staff have to accept the new role or take severance? Will each person get a one-on-one meeting? How does "same pay or higher" get set for each person?

5. **Where do people take questions?** Is there a named HR contact, a staff meeting, or an FAQ?

If you don't know some of these yet, say so. I'll leave those parts out rather than guess.

1. I don't know yet who it goes to or whether the 14 will hear first in person.

2. Pay in the center starts $1.50 an hour above current teller pay. Work from home two days a week after 90 days of training. People with the most years here pick shifts first, but I can't promise anyone 9 to 5. For members, the gain is shorter hold times than the current 9 minutes. I don't have a specific gain for the other five branches. And you're right that "better for everyone" goes past what I can show. I'm fine saying what's true instead.

3. The center is at our main office on Elm Avenue. I don't know when it opens or when training starts.

4. Written offers go out by February 14, and decisions are due March 1. Anyone who wants a one-on-one with HR gets one. Anyone who takes the new role and wants out within 6 months can still get the severance.

5. I don't know beyond the HR one-on-ones.

I wrote this so it works whether it goes to all staff or only the 14. It speaks to the affected staff directly and has one line at the end for everyone else.

<final_document>
Subject: Maple Street and Route 9 branches closing March 31

Team,

I'm writing to share a decision that affects our Maple Street and Route 9 branches and the 14 people who work there.

On March 31, we will close both branches. Every person who works at them will be offered a job in a new member phone and chat center at our main office on Elm Avenue, at the same pay or higher.

**Why we're doing this**

The way our members reach us has changed. Over the last three years, visits to Maple Street and Route 9 fell 44%. Across the credit union, phone and chat contacts rose 60%. We haven't kept up, and members calling us now wait an average of 9 minutes on hold. The center puts experienced people where members are actually trying to reach us.

**What the new role looks like**

- Pay starts $1.50 an hour above current teller pay.
- The center is open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. Shifts will rotate. People with the most years here choose shifts first, but I can't promise anyone a 9-to-5 schedule.
- After 90 days of training, you can work from home two days a week.

I know the change in hours is a real cost for some of you, especially if your life is built around a 9-to-5 day. I'd rather say that plainly than pretend otherwise.

**What happens next**

- Written offers go out by February 14.
- Decisions are due March 1.
- If you'd like a one-on-one with HR to talk through your situation, you'll get one. Just ask HR.
- If you decide not to take the new role, you'll receive two weeks of pay for every year you've worked here.
- If you take the new role and find within six months that it isn't right for you, you can still leave with that same severance.

We'll share the center's opening date and training schedule as soon as they're set.

To everyone at Maple Street and Route 9: thank you. Many of our members have known you by name for years, and that knowledge is exactly what they'll need on the other end of the line. To everyone else: you'll be working alongside these colleagues in new ways, and I'm asking you to help make this move a good one.

[Your name]
Chief Operating Officer
</final_document>

A few notes:

- **Tell the 14 first if you can.** Ideally their managers or you tell them in person before this email goes out. If that happens, you could add a line near the top like "As many of you heard from your managers today…".
- **The claim that it makes everyone's job better is gone.** In its place, the email names the specific gains: higher pay, working from home, and shorter waits for members. It also admits the cost of the new hours. Staff are more likely to believe the good parts when the email is honest about the hard part.
- **Fill in later:** the center's opening date and training start, and an HR contact name or email if you want something more specific than "ask HR."
